ledger.claim: The deviation is established on the platform's own recorded distances: the trip record gives an actual distance of 9.9 km against a recommended route of 8.3 km, a deviation of 1.60 km, which is over POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance and is recorded as not within tolerance. This is not a within-tolerance case, so the driver cannot rely on POL-RD-24 rows (c) or (e) to keep the whole fare.

POL-RD-21 required the driver to inform the rider of the deviation by in-app chat before or at the point of deviation. The complete chat log holds exactly two messages, at 18:21:17 and 18:21:57, both about the pickup ('waiting at the library drop-off', 'thanks coming'), and the deviation was detected later at 18:27:35. The driver had a working, read-and-answered in-app channel minutes earlier and said nothing about the reroute on it.

The trip record carries an empty in_app_calls list, so the driver's account of a verbal notice has no call recording behind it. Under POL-RD-21 a verbal notice with no recording cannot be established, and under POL-GEN-26 no inference may be drawn from that absence. The notification obligation therefore fails on this record.

The traffic justification is not made out on POL-RD-23's terms. POL-RD-23 justifies a reroute only where a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window; the advisory's own derived facts leave the route intersection undetermined (intersects_route: null, with the express reason that 'the record does not say whether this advisory lies on the recommended route'), so the intersection element is not established and the reroute is not traffic-justified.

In the alternative, even taking the driver's traffic case at its highest, POL-RD-24 row (b) governs: traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation over 1 km, which prescribes a refund of the excess distance fare rather than retention. Row (a) — the only row that withholds money — requires that the rider was informed and agreed, and the chat log shows no notification and no agreement, so row (a) is unavailable to the driver.

The prescribed remedy is arithmetically the present state. The excess distance fare is the deviation of 1.60 km times the per-km rate of 1.05 SGD, without surge, rounded to the cent: 1.68 SGD (POL-RD-24). The fare breakdown records refund_issued_sgd of 1.68 SGD against a PARTIALLY_REFUNDED fare, so both row (b) and row (d) are already satisfied. The driver's claim for that 1.68 SGD fails and the present state stands — the rider keeps the refund (NO_ACTION under POL-GEN-03).

The driver's stated reason — that the detour was 'faster for him' — is contradicted by the trip record itself: the actual duration was 21.0 minutes against a recommended-route duration of 17.6 minutes. The deviation cost the rider time as well as distance, so it cannot be excused as a service to the rider, and the driver's own account of a beneficial reroute is unsupported by the platform's timings.

This case is within the AI's remit and should be decided now rather than held: the deviation of 1.60 km is within POL-RD-25's 2 km limit for an AI ruling, and the contested value of 1.68 SGD sits below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band so the ruling is final at any confidence, with no fraud flag on either profile to raise the bar. The refund should therefore be confirmed rather than left in suspense.

The reroute was traffic-justified on this record. EV-ADVIS-05016-01 records HEAVY_TRAFFIC on Central Expressway (CTE), direction towards SLE, location 'after Bukit Timah Road exit to Braddell Road', valid 17:57-19:12, which covers the trip window (18:22-18:43), and HEAVY_TRAFFIC is an admissible congestion type under POL-RD-23. The recommended route for this trip was Victoria Street, Central Expressway (CTE), Braddell Road, Upper Thomson Road, and the trip record's own route_deviation_detected event fixes the point of departure at 'CTE / Bukit Timah Road exit'. The advisory therefore sits on the stretch of the CTE that the recommended route itself uses between the Bukit Timah Road exit and Braddell Road - the road immediately ahead of the vehicle when it turned off, and the stretch the driver's trace shows it left. The artifact's intersects_route field is null and POL-RD-23 leaves that question to the Judge on the advisory's road, direction and location; on those three facts it resolves on the recommended route. Rerouting in response to congestion is exactly what POL-RD-21 permits, so row (d) of POL-RD-24 (not traffic-justified) does not fit this trip.

The driver cannot be charged more than the excess distance fare, and that sum has already been taken. POL-RD-24 fixes the excess distance fare at deviation_km x fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd with no surge: 1.60 km x 1.05 SGD = 1.68 SGD, rounded to the cent. EV-FARE-05016 shows precisely 1.68 SGD refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver as a fare_adjusted event at 2026-09-08T00:23:37+08:00, with payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED. The platform has therefore already collected the whole of the only amount the matrix authorises for a justified deviation beyond tolerance; the 26.34 SGD metered fare is not in issue and no further recovery from the driver is warranted.

The driver does not put his case on notification, because the record does not carry it. The chat log EV-CHAT-05016 is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 and holds only two messages, both sent before the trip began and neither about the route, and trip_record.in_app_calls is empty; POL-RD-21 accordingly leaves no in-app chat and no call recording showing that the deviation was notified or acknowledged, and the driver's own account of not waking a sleeping rider is a reason for silence, not a notice. The case therefore falls in row (b) of POL-RD-24, whose entire remedy is the 1.68 SGD excess distance fare that has already been refunded, and the driver's request that that sum be returned to him is not supported on this record.

ruling.explanation:
Mr Driver, you drove a different way (Bukit Timah Road, Adam Road, Lornie Road) from the recommended route (CTE and Braddell Road). On the platform's own recorded distances the detour was 1.60 km (9.9 km driven against 8.3 km recommended), which is over the 1.0 km tolerance and under the 2 km ceiling at which an AI must hand the case to a human (POL-RD-22, POL-RD-25). Your reason for the detour is borne out: the LTA record reports HEAVY_TRAFFIC on the CTE towards SLE, from after the Bukit Timah Road exit to Braddell Road, 17:57-19:12, which overlaps the trip window and lies on the stretch of the CTE the recommended route itself uses, so the reroute is traffic-justified under POL-RD-23. What the rules also require is that you tell the rider before or at the point you turned off (POL-RD-21). The complete in-app chat for this trip holds only the two pickup messages, at 18:21:17 and 18:21:57, and the turn-off was detected at 18:27:35; the trip record's call list is empty, so a spoken notice cannot be established (POL-GEN-26), and the rider's account that you never mentioned a route change is consistent with that. That puts the case in row (b) of the refund matrix - traffic-justified, rider not informed, detour over 1 km - whose remedy is the excess distance fare and nothing more (POL-RD-24). That figure is 1.60 km x the 1.05 SGD per-km rate = 1.68 SGD. The fare ledger shows exactly 1.68 SGD already refunded to the rider and recovered from your earnings, with the fare left PARTIALLY_REFUNDED, so the only sum the matrix authorises has already moved. Rider, you keep that 1.68 SGD; the remainder of the 26.34 SGD metered fare is not in issue. Mr Driver, your filing asks for that 1.68 SGD back, and on this record it is not owed to you. The outcome on your filing is therefore NO_ACTION and the present state stands, with no further money moved in either direction. The disputed value (1.68 SGD) is below the 10.00 SGD band, neither profile carries a fraud flag, and the 0.80 confidence this category requires is met, so the AI may decide this finally. The detour took 21.0 minutes against a recommended 17.6 minutes, but trip duration does not enter the refund matrix and does not change the result. A route deviation has no referral clause, so none is issued.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
